headline.headline: PISTONS FORCE GAME 7, CUNNINGHAM TAKES OVER IN SECOND HALF STUNNER
headline.deck: Detroit's young star erupts as Pistons blow out top-seeded Cavaliers to survive elimination
headline.body:
CLEVELAND — Cade Cunningham had seen enough. Down at halftime and staring at elimination in the Eastern Conference semifinals, the Detroit Pistons' franchise cornerstone took the floor in the second half Friday night and dismantled the Cleveland Cavaliers piece by piece, scoring 21 points and orchestrating a dominant second-half surge that carried the Pistons to a 115-94 victory and forced a winner-take-all Game 7.

The top-seeded Pistons, who entered the series as the conference's best team and then stumbled badly enough to reach the brink of elimination, looked nothing like a team in trouble once Cunningham locked in. Detroit outscored Cleveland by a stunning margin in the third quarter, turning a contest the Cavaliers believed they controlled into a rout that left Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse stunned and silent. The Pistons' defense suffocated Cleveland's perimeter shooters while Cunningham found open cutters and knocked down mid-range jumpers with clockwork efficiency.

Game 7 tips off Sunday in Detroit, where the Pistons have been nearly unbeatable all season. Cleveland will turn to its own star talent to answer, but after Friday's performance it is Cunningham and the Pistons who carry the momentum. One game, winner advances. Loser goes home.

secondary.headline: ASHBY STANDS ALONE AS BASEBALL'S ONLY 8-GAME WINNER
secondary.deck: Milwaukee left-hander reaches historic milestone with help from a bizarre interference call
secondary.body:
MILWAUKEE — Aaron Ashby made history Friday night at American Family Field, becoming the first pitcher in the major leagues to win eight games this season as the Milwaukee Brewers edged the Minnesota Twins 3-2 in a game that turned on one of the stranger plays of the young season. Ashby worked through a quality start against a Twins lineup that entered the evening among the hottest in the American League, and he was bailed out in a critical moment when a Twins third baseman was called for interference, a ruling that changed the complexion of the inning and ultimately preserved the victory.

The win further cements Ashby as the early frontrunner in the National League Cy Young conversation. No other starter in baseball has reached the eight-win mark, and with Milwaukee surging in the NL Central standings the Brewers are quietly positioning themselves as one of the more dangerous clubs in the senior circuit heading into summer.

secondary.headline: MINNESOTA PLAYED ITS ENTIRE SECOND-ROUND SERIES WITHOUT BRODIN AND ERIKSSON EK
secondary.deck: Wild's two key players battled broken bones in their feet as the team fought deep into the playoffs
secondary.body:
ST. PAUL — The Minnesota Wild were already undermanned and nobody outside the locker room knew just how badly. Defenseman Jonas Brodin and center Joel Eriksson Ek both missed the team's second-round playoff series after suffering broken bones in their feet, the organization confirmed Friday, revealing the full extent of the injury toll the Wild absorbed while competing in the NHL's most brutal month. The disclosures reframe Minnesota's postseason run in a striking light and raise pointed questions about the depth of the franchise's roster construction.

Brodin anchors one of the league's better defensive pairings when healthy, and Eriksson Ek's two-way play at center is considered essential to the Wild's structure in all three zones. Playing without both for an entire second-round series represents an extraordinary challenge for any NHL club. The news arrives as the second round continues across the league, with surviving teams now pushing toward conference finals berths.

secondary.headline: FORMER NFL LINEMAN JOSH MAURO DIED FROM DRUG COMBINATION, MEDICAL EXAMINER CONFIRMS
secondary.deck: Fentanyl, cocaine and ethanol intoxication ruled cause of death for the defensive lineman
secondary.body:
Former NFL defensive lineman Josh Mauro died from an acute combination of fentanyl, cocaine and ethanol intoxication, according to the medical examiner's findings released Friday. Mauro, who played for several franchises during his professional career, was remembered by former teammates and coaches following news of the cause of death. The disclosure adds Mauro's name to a devastating list of professional athletes whose lives have been claimed by the fentanyl crisis that has spread across the country.

The NFL and its player safety programs have increasingly confronted the challenge of substance dependency among current and former players, though critics argue the league has moved too slowly to provide comprehensive mental health and addiction resources to players after their careers end. Mauro's death is a sobering reminder of the dangers that persist long after the final whistle, and his former colleagues called Friday for expanded support systems for retired players navigating life away from the game.

column.headline: GAME 7 IS BASKETBALL AT ITS PUREST — AND DETROIT EARNED EVERY BIT OF THIS MOMENT
column.body:
There is no better regular-season record, no more favorable seeding, no home-court advantage that fully prepares a team for the weight of a Game 7. The Detroit Pistons spent the first six games of this Eastern Conference semifinal series reminding everyone that regular-season dominance does not travel automatically into the playoffs. And then, when the lights were brightest and elimination loomed, Cade Cunningham reminded everyone why the Pistons were the conference's top seed in the first place. That is the playoff contract. You must earn it twice.

Sunday in Detroit will be one of the most-watched games of this entire postseason, and rightfully so. The Cavaliers are not done. They have the talent and the motivation of a team that let a close-out game slip away on their own floor. But this series has Cunningham's fingerprints all over it now, and that is a dangerous thing for Cleveland to carry into a building that has been a fortress all year. A franchise that has waited years to matter again is one win from the conference finals. The city of Detroit knows how to wait. The question is whether the Pistons can finish.

story.headline: REDS HAMMER NATIONALS 15-1 IN HISTORIC ROUT
story.deck: Cincinnati explodes for 15 runs, handing Washington its most lopsided loss of the young season
story.body:
CINCINNATI — The Cincinnati Reds turned Thursday afternoon at Great American Ball Park into a full-scale demolition job, pounding the Washington Nationals 15-1 in a performance that left little doubt which club belongs among the National League's elite. The Reds sent 11 men to the plate in at least one inning and worked through the Nationals bullpen like a buzz saw, collecting hits in bunches from top to bottom in a lineup that showed no mercy.

The carnage was spread across every corner of the Cincinnati order. The Reds drew walks, collected extra-base hits and kept the pressure relentless from the opening inning, chasing Washington's starter before the fourth frame and making short work of every reliever the Nationals offered in relief. Washington's lone run did little more than prevent the shutout, as the deficit ballooned well beyond salvageable territory before the middle innings arrived.

The rout capped a busy Thursday slate that saw the Milwaukee Brewers blank the San Diego Padres 7-1 and the Seattle Mariners manhandle the Houston Astros 8-3 in a statement win in the AL West. But no result matched Cincinnati's sheer offensive volume, a 14-run margin that served notice across the Senior Circuit that the Reds are playing their best baseball of the 2026 season.

story.headline: CUNNINGHAM CARRIES PISTONS PAST CAVS TO FORCE WINNER-TAKE-ALL GAME 7
story.deck: Detroit dominates second half in 115-94 rout, setting up Sunday showdown in Cleveland.
story.body:
Cade Cunningham scored 21 points and the top-seeded Detroit Pistons turned a competitive game into a blowout Friday night, beating the Cleveland Cavaliers 115-94 to force a decisive Game 7 in their Eastern Conference semifinal series. The Pistons, who trailed at halftime, came out of the locker room like a different team and systematically dismantled Cleveland's defense, outscoring the Cavaliers by more than 20 points in the second half alone.

Cunningham was at his commanding best down the stretch, orchestrating the Pistons offense with crisp pick-and-roll decisions and attacking a fatigued Cleveland defense that had no answer for Detroit's pace or precision. Donovan Mitchell, who has shouldered the offensive load for the Cavaliers throughout this series, was held in check during the crucial third quarter when the game slipped away from Cleveland for good.

Game 7 tips off Sunday in Cleveland, where the Cavaliers will lean on a raucous Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse crowd to shake off the sting of Friday's collapse. Detroit, meanwhile, has now won back-to-back elimination games and carries genuine momentum into what figures to be one of the most electric nights of the 2026 playoffs. A berth in the Eastern Conference Finals awaits whichever team survives.

story.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS STRIPPED OF PICK, FINED AFTER COACH TORTORELLA'S MEDIA FRACAS ROCKS PLAYOFF FIELD
story.deck: NHL punishes Vegas with lost draft pick and $100,000 fine as conference finals loom
story.body:
The NHL dropped a stunning disciplinary hammer on the Vegas Golden Knights on Thursday, stripping the franchise of a second-round draft pick and fining head coach John Tortorella $100,000 after the team was found to have boxed out media from access during the playoffs. The punishment, swift and severe, lands just as Vegas prepares to face the Colorado Avalanche in the Western Conference Finals, casting a dark shadow over what promised to be a marquee matchup.

The penalty against Tortorella, one of the league's most combustible and celebrated coaches, marks a rare instance of the NHL acting forcefully against a contending club mid-postseason. Tortorella has never been a stranger to controversy, but the loss of a draft pick represents tangible long-term damage to the franchise's ability to replenish talent. Golden Knights general manager Kelly McCrimmon had no immediate public comment, leaving Tortorella to answer questions his club's own conduct had invited.

On the ice Thursday, playoff action continued to sharpen the field. Final scores saw one team win 6-3 and another 5-1 in results that underscored the relentless pace of second-round competition. But those results were quickly overshadowed by the league office's announcement in New York, which sent shockwaves through every remaining playoff locker room and reminded the sport that conduct off the ice carries consequences just as steep as those on it.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Three veteran signal-callers find new homes as contenders retool for 2026.
story.body:
The NFL landscape shifted dramatically this spring as a wave of quarterback movement reshaped expectations across the league. Sam Darnold, coming off a career-best season with the Minnesota Vikings, agreed to a four-year, $168 million contract with the Las Vegas Raiders, giving the long-struggling franchise a legitimate starter for the first time in years. The deal, finalized late last month, signals a full organizational commitment from Raiders brass to build around the 28-year-old after years of carousel-style roster construction.

Meanwhile, the New England Patriots made the most aggressive move of the offseason by trading three draft picks to the Cleveland Browns for veteran quarterback Joe Flacco, pairing the 41-year-old journeyman with a young and hungry Patriots roster rebuilt under second-year head coach Mike Vrabel. General manager Eliot Wolf called Flacco a bridge option while the team evaluates its long-term options at the position, with the 2026 draft class considered deep at quarterback. The trade drew mixed reviews from analysts, many of whom questioned whether Flacco could hold up through a full season.

On the draft front, teams spent the pre-draft process zeroing in on Colorado wide receiver and consensus first-round prospect Marcus Bell, whose combination of size and route-running drew comparisons to a young Davante Adams. The Jacksonville Jaguars, holding the fourth overall pick, worked out Bell three times according to league sources, suggesting the organization is prepared to pivot away from its long-standing need at offensive tackle. The NFL Draft kicks off in Pittsburgh on April 23, and league executives expect quarterback and pass-rusher to dominate the top ten selections.
